rgb: The setting is outdoors next to a small blue-and-white booth decorated with dark palm-tree designs; in the first frame, a sandy parking area and parked vehicles about 15 to 30 metres away appear on the right. Straight ahead of the camera wearer, roughly 0.5 to 1 metre away, is a white-framed sliding window with its left side open and its right side shut, the glass reflecting the open landscape behind. Within the dim booth, around 1 to 1.5 metres away, a person wearing a light blue shirt sits below the wearer’s eye level behind the open left window, facing forward and slightly down at papers and a clipboard on an interior counter within arm’s reach instead of looking up toward the wearer. The booth wall and window frame block the person’s lower body and left side, and the right glass pane partly conceals the interior. From the first frame to the second, the wearer turns their head to the left and takes a small step closer, centering the window in view; this shifts the parking lot on the right out of sight while revealing the booth’s palm-painted left corner and the pebbled ground beneath. During frames 2 through 5, the wearer stays still within arm’s reach of the lower windowsill, about 0.4 to 0.6 metres away, and reaches forward with their right hand to hold a dark rectangular object directly on the sill in front of the seated person.
depth: The depth map depicts the wall of a small outdoor booth directly ahead of the camera wearer, approximately 0.4–0.8 m away and shown in bright white. A sliding-window opening occupies the right side in frames 2–5, while frame 1 shows an open parking area, barrier poles, and cars far back on the right, about 10–25 m away and rendered dark grey or black. Between frames 1 and 2, the wearer turns left and moves slightly nearer the booth wall while reaching their right hand and a handheld device, roughly 0.3–0.4 m away, into the bottom of the open left window pane. The hand and device then remain within arm’s reach of both the wearer and a seated person inside, who is around 0.8–1.2 m from the wearer and approximately 0.4–0.6 m behind the wearer’s hand. The map clearly distinguishes the nearby window frame and projecting hand/device outline from the recessed interior, whose distance is more difficult to assess in the RGB strip’s dark, shadowy booth. However, depth readings inside the open left window are unreliable: the interior and much of the seated person appear pitch black at nearly infinite depth. The map also interprets the reflective right glass pane as a solid surface at the wall’s depth and produces a spurious bright depth blob over the privacy-blur artifact on the window frame in frames 2 and 3.
segmentation: The segmentation output detects the seated person within the lower-left window in frames 1, 4, and 5, approximately 0.8–1.2 m away; two parked cars in frame 1’s right background, about 15–25 m distant; the camera wearer’s outstretched right hand at the bottom center-right in frames 2–5, roughly 0.3–0.4 m away and classified as “person”; and the handheld black item as a “cell phone” in frame 5. As the camera turns left from the parking lot toward the booth wall between frame 1 and frames 2–5, the cars disappear from the right side of the view and the wearer’s hand comes into view at the bottom windowsill. It remains approximately 0.4–0.6 m ahead of and slightly below the seated person’s torso. The person is partly blocked by the left window frame and looks downward toward papers on a desk rather than at the wearer. In frames 1, 4, and 5, the masks distinguish the dimly illuminated seated person from the booth’s dark interior and separate the wearer’s hand from the sill. However, segmentation is unreliable in frames 2 and 3, completely failing to detect the seated person inside the window, probably because of the vertical privacy blur along the window edge. It also misses the handheld device in frames 2–4 and does not include the booth structure, papers, or barrier poles.
pose: The pose output finds upper-body landmarks—yellow shoulder and head/face points—for the person seated in the booth at the lower left of frame 1, about 0.8–1.2 m away. It also follows the camera wearer’s extended right wrist and hand at the bottom of the windowsill, approximately 0.3–0.4 m away, throughout frames 2–5. In frame 1, the seated person’s shoulder alignment and lowered head landmarks show that they face forward-right toward the desk and look down rather than toward the camera wearer. Across frames 2–5, the wearer’s hand stays motionless at arm’s reach on the lower window frame, with the thumb pointing upward and the fingers wrapped around the handheld object. The magenta hand skeletons in frames 3 and 5 reveal detailed, 3D-like finger positioning and the orientation of the wearer’s grip, which is partly lost in shadow against the dark device in RGB. However, pose detection for the seated person is very unreliable in frames 2–5, entirely omitting their body and hands while they remain in shadow behind the window frame. For the wearer’s unchanged hand, it also switches inconsistently between rough yellow body-and-wrist landmarks in frames 2 and 4 and complete magenta hand skeletons in frames 3 and 5.
